clusters.state_of_play: Martha Lillard, 78, the last known U.S. polio patient living in an iron lung, died on 26 June in Oklahoma. COVID-19 had previously worsened her condition, leaving her dependent on the device nearly 24 hours a day.

clusters.state_of_play: FBI Director Kash Patel faces bipartisan scrutiny: Senate Judiciary Chair Grassley sent a letter in May demanding reimbursement records for personal use of FBI aircraft and answers on BMW purchases — later revealed publicly by Rep. Jamie Raskin and Sen. Dick Durbin. Patel is also accused of demanding personal perks including snorkeling and jet ski trips, straining the bureau. Patel has publicly responded, bizarrely claiming his jet ski is 'gold plated.' Separately, Sen. Mark Warner wrote to Patel and Acting AG Blanche after MS NOW reported Patel ordered 260 FBI intelligence analysts from field offices nationwide to investigate the 2020 election, which Warner called a 'fool's errand.' Senate Democrats had also previously written to Blanche and Patel over the Georgia FBI personnel surge. Now, two Atlanta-based FBI analysts — a married couple — have been fired after they raised concerns that the Fulton County 2020 election investigation was thin on evidence and, per MS NOW, refused to join the probe on grounds they believed it unjustified.

clusters.state_of_play: Shabir Ahmed, ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang, has been released and Pakistan is refusing to take him back. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. The Reform UK/Farage financial scrutiny story continues: the £5m crypto donor is now linked to Tether, a giant and secretive cryptocurrency firm that Farage has publicly championed. Separately, Farage refused taxpayer-funded security as inadequate, with Reform UK continuing to fund his personal protection.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, a major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes; fire services were tackling 19 separate wildfires across the UK in the latest official update. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura, adding to a series of corruption allegations facing Sánchez's family and the PSOE.

Europe is experiencing its third wave of extreme heat this summer, with at least 12 killed in a Spanish wildfire and wildfires burning across the continent; Germany faces another scorching week though no records are expected; the UK has extended an Amber heat health alert as parts enter a second week of temperatures above the heatwave threshold, with 'exceptional' wildfire risk flagged, two swimmers found dead, and the Met Office warning the heatwave will last until at least next week with a thunderstorm risk developing in the south. clusters.state_of_play: Police have arrested two people suspected of deliberately starting the Fontainebleau forest fire, which has now scorched more than 1,900 hectares south of Paris — up from earlier estimates of ~1,200 hectares. Investigators found ten ignition points near the fire's origin, reinforcing the conclusion that the blaze was intentional. Officials have described the blaze as of 'exceptional scale', with hundreds of residents evacuated and road and rail links disrupted. Some 400 firefighters and two waterbombing aircraft have been deployed. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had already raised the possibility of deliberate ignition; the arrests and the discovery of multiple ignition points mark significant developments in that probe. The fire coincides with France's third heatwave since May, which has forced early closures of the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Musée d'Orsay, and led many towns to cancel Bastille Day fireworks displays due to elevated fire risk.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, a major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes; fire services were tackling 19 separate wildfires across the UK in the latest official update. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura, adding to a series of corruption allegations facing Sánchez's family and the PSOE.
